previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with stage IV cholangiocarcinoma in remission and a history of recurrent cholangitis, was admitted with fever, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. He was found to have E. coli bacteremia likely originating from the biliary tract, with imaging confirming persistent cholangitis and worsening biliary ductal dilation. Due to rising liver enzymes, he underwent an ERCP which revealed and cleared sludge and stone fragments from the bile ducts. He was treated with IV meropenem, and a PICC line was placed for continued outpatient antibiotic therapy. His pancytopenia, likely due to infection-related bone marrow suppression, was monitored without specific intervention. He improved clinically, remained afebrile, and was discharged home with a two-week course of IV antibiotics, follow-up arranged with infectious disease and gastroenterology, and instructions to hold his probiotic until further guidance.

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with recurrent cholangitis admitted with fever.//
Assess patency of biliary tree.

TECHNIQUE:  T1- and T2-weighted multiplanar images of the abdomen were
acquired in a 1.5 T magnet.
Intravenous contrast: 8 mL Gadavist.
Oral contrast:  1 cc of Gadavist mixed with 50 cc of water was administered
for oral contrast.

COMPARISON:  Liver/gallbladder ultrasound ___.
MRCP ___
CT abdomen/pelvis contrast ___.

FINDINGS: 

Lower Thorax: Limited evaluation of the lung bases is notable for bibasilar
atelectasis.  No pleural or pericardial effusion.

Liver: Previously noted parenchymal hepatic hyper enhancement involving the
right hepatic lobe is overall unchanged since prior examination.  The
periductal enhancement involving the left hepatic lobe, however, has near
completely resolved consistent with resolving cholangitis.  (1301:41).  Again
noted is an ill-defined T1 hypointense area at the confluence of the hepatic
ducts with arterial hyper enhancement and no washout which is stable since
prior.  No signal drop on out of phase imaging to suggest hepatic steatosis. 
No intrahepatic abscess.  There are multiple scattered arterially
hyperenhancing foci without correlate on additional sequences consistent
transient hepatic intensity differences.

Biliary: There is persistent mild right and moderate left intrahepatic biliary
duct dilatation, unchanged since ___. Two common bile duct stents are
again noted with pneumobilia.

Pancreas: There is diffuse pancreatic atrophy with top-normal pancreatic duct
with 2 new apparent filling defects within the main pancreatic duct which
bloom on the inphase imaging consistent with air.  No definite
pancreaticolith.  (10:23).  Few subcentimeter pancreatic cystic lesions are
again noted largest measuring up to a 0.2 cm within the pancreatic tail, for
which no additional follow-up is warranted as per departmental guidelines
given patient's age.  No pancreatic mass.  No peripancreatic fat stranding.

Spleen: Spleen is enlarged measuring 15.6 cm.  No suspicious mass.  A 2.2 cm
accessory spleen is noted.  Trace perisplenic free fluid noted.

Adrenal Glands: Bilateral adrenal glands are symmetric in size without
discrete nodule.

Kidneys: There are bilateral T2 hyperintense nonenhancing simple renal cysts. 
Kidneys are otherwise homogeneous in signal intensity without suspicious mass.
No hydronephrosis or perinephric fat stranding.

Gastrointestinal Tract:  Distal esophagus, stomach, visualized small and large
bowel are unremarkable.  No obstruction.

Lymph Nodes: Retroperitoneal and mesenteric lymph nodes are nonenlarged.

Vasculature: No abdominal aortic aneurysm.  Celiac axis, bilateral renal
arteries, SMA, and proximal ___ are patent.  There is persistent severe
attenuation of the left portal vein.

Osseous and Soft Tissue Structures: No suspicious osseous lesions.  Soft
tissues are unremarkable.

IMPRESSION: 

1.  Resolving cholangitis involving the left intrahepatic bile ducts with
persistent cholangitis involving the right hepatic lobe.  No intrahepatic
abscess.  No fluid collection
2.  Persistent moderate left and mild right intrahepatic biliary duct
dilatation with abnormal parenchymal signal and enhancement of the confluence
of hepatic ducts likely related to posttreatment inflammatory fibrosis. 
Underlying tumor cannot be excluded.  No new stricture.
3.  Stable splenomegaly.
4.  Air within the main pancreatic duct, likely related to biliary stent
placement
